summary.headline: M&M Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 25% to ₹4,588 crore on revenue of ₹57,553 crore, with full-year tractor industry outlook cut to flattish.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 25% to ₹57,553 crore and PAT rose 25% to ₹4,588 crore, with year-to-date profit up 29% and ROE at 21%. Growth came from multiple businesses (Logistics turnaround, Accelo, Mahindra Finance, Tech M, Growth Gems) while Farm fell 9% on a festive-season shift and weak international subsidiaries. Management cut its full-year tractor industry outlook from +5% to flattish, citing a weaker monsoon (87% of LPA vs 90% earlier) and drought in Maharashtra and Karnataka. Auto demand remains supply-constrained, with waiting periods of 5–7 months on Scorpio-N and XUV 7XO, and capacity is set to rise from 66,000 to 82,000 units/month this year and 92,000 next year.

segments.name: Auto (SUV, LCV, EV)
segments.commentary: PAT up 55% with SUV and LCV volumes strong; ICE capacity 61k and EV 8k reached 73k+ units in October, with EV penetration at 12–12.7% of SUVs. Prices raised 5% in Auto to offset commodity inflation.

segments.name: Farm (tractors)
segments.commentary: Profit down 9% on festive-season shift, weak monsoon and international drag; Farm prices raised 4%. Full-year industry tractor outlook cut to flattish from +5%; the three global subsidiaries face US -15%, Brazil -18%, Turkey -36%.

segments.name: Mahindra Finance
segments.commentary: PAT up 61% (after 55% last quarter) on lower asset quality and tech/data gains; AUM above ₹1,30,000 crore against ₹65,000 crore starting point.

segments.name: Tech Mahindra
segments.commentary: PAT up 33%, with large deal wins and a strong pipeline; AI adoption accelerating.

segments.name: Logistics and Growth Gems
segments.commentary: Logistics turned from loss-making last year to a good profit level; Growth Gems profit up 3X again, Accelo up 70%.

segments.name: Last Mile Mobility (Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, Suman Mishra)
segments.commentary: Capacity capped; ~45,000 units in quarter, all electric. Industry 3W electrification at 45–50%, with L5M estimated at 70%+; capacity up 25% over last 1.5 years and further expansion planned.

segments.name: Aerospace (Mahindra Aerostructures)
segments.commentary: Order book growing; new Airbus A320neo skin/fuselage tail package won, plus single-source helicopter fuselage supply. Management targets $1bn annual orders by FY30 and says it is at 28X the base.

segments.name: Lifespaces
segments.commentary: Pre-sales reached 5X of the decade target (14X). Bhandup project spans 35–37 acres; capital deployed only once profitability was confirmed.

guidance_outlook: Tractor industry full-year FY27 outlook cut to flattish from +5%; the cut is for the full year, not only H2, with H2 implying about -10%.
Mahindra SUV industry outlook maintained at mid-to-high teens growth.
LCV industry outlook raised to double-digit growth.

Auto capacity to reach 82,000 units/month this year (+27%), then 92,000 next year; Chakan NU_IQ adds about 8,000 and EV goes to 12,000 by Feb–March 2027, with a new Nagpur plant (1,500–2,000 acres) on track.
Five major launches by June 2027 including first NU_IQ product, Lifestyler, a significant refresh and an LCV.
Management reiterates 15–20% EPS growth and 18% ROE target; PLI to fade over time and EV margins to converge toward ICE over a longer journey.
Management expects core tractor pressure in Q3, improvement in Q4, and normalcy in FY28; Q3 has steel/rubber upticks but precious metals falling.
capex_capacity: Auto capacity 66,000 units/month today, 82,000 by end-FY27, 92,000 next year, and 132,000 by FY31 with the new plant.
Nagpur plant: first-phase land acquired; committed to buy 1,500–2,000 acres; supplier park land also bought.
EV capacity 8,000 to 12,000 by Feb–March 2027; NU_IQ capacity addition of about 8,000–10,000 at Chakan.
Last mile mobility capacity capped; multiple actions underway to add capacity and a new full platform (at least double footprint) under evaluation.
Aerospace: second plant running, third plant under construction.
demand_pricing: Auto demand is strong across brands; waiting periods are 5–7 months for Scorpio-N and XUV 7XO, and about 1.5–2 months for most other products.

Shift in powertrain mix: away from petrol toward CNG, EV and, surprisingly, diesel; the company says the festive season saw no slowdown in SUVs, including in rural areas, except in parts of the South.
EV cumulative sales above 1 lakh; 9S is the highest-selling EV; BE 6 launched 15 August.
Auto prices raised by 5%, Farm by 4%; management says pricing has not hurt demand.
Management stopped sharing order book data because of cancellation noise.

qa_highlights.question: How has demand shaped up after the GST cut, and what changed in powertrain mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand stayed robust with no SUV slowdown in rural areas; petrol has lost share to CNG, EV and diesel. Vahan like-for-like festive volumes were roughly flat to minus, and M&M is the fastest-growing brand on Vahan.

qa_highlights.question: Is M&M planning capacity for full utilisation given structural shortages?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity went from 17,000 five years ago to 66,000 now and will be 82,000 at year end and 92,000 next year; a Nagpur plant and a supplier park will double capacity with room to expand quickly.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for EV demand after fuel prices fall, and localisation of batteries?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says EV adoption has passed a tunnelling inflection; pump prices are unlikely to fall soon. Battery packs are already localised; cells will be sourced overseas unless captive supply is needed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tractor outlook for next year given monsoon normalisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects NOAA's normal monsoon probability above 70% next year and a flat industry even in a strong El Niño year; the Navratri shift will support Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How much PLI was booked and what is the EV margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹1,000 crore PLI booked this quarter. EV margins are around 9% helped by PLI; management expects volume, supplier leverage and pricing power to take margins toward ICE levels over time, with depreciation the main drag.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for international Farm subsidiaries after exits?
qa_highlights.answer: Sampo and Erkunt exits are complete; Mitsubishi Mahindra Agricultural Machinery Japan closes by Q4. Exit costs from 3Q and 4Q last year will not recur, helping Farm consolidation in H2.

risks_watch: Tractor industry outlook cut to flattish; monsoon at 87% of LPA with drought in Maharashtra and Karnataka; reservoir levels low.
Commodity inflation: steel up 17% YoY, copper up 42%, rubber up 40%; management flagged possible upticks in steel and rubber in Q3.
International Farm subsidiaries (US -15%, Brazil -18%, Turkey -36%) remain under industry stress.
EV margin depends on PLI support (~₹1,000 crore this quarter) and faces depreciation burden from new investments.
Possible inventory correction in tractor channel in Q4 as industry adjusts to slower demand.
Capacity constraints may limit near-term volume and share gains until NU_IQ, EV and Nagpur capacity comes on stream.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the headline quarter and long-term targets, but cautious on tractors and commodities. Management cut the full-year tractor outlook, said the challenges are not yet over, and was reluctant to share order books or product-level capacity.
key_quotes: The keyword for this quarter is resilience.
What we have always said is 15% to 20% EPS growth and 18% RoE.
We've reduced the outlook for the year.
Demand for all our brands at the moment is extremely strong, EV and ICE.

growth.why: Management guides SUV industry mid-to-high teens and LCV double-digit growth with auto capacity rising from 66k to 82k units/month by end-FY27 (+27%) and 92k in FY28, backed by specific capacity additions (Chakan NU_IQ, EV to 12k, Nagpur plant) and 5-7 month waiting periods; tractor industry outlook was cut to flattish, which offsets growth in farm.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated margin 8.8% in Q2 vs 7.7% in Q1 and about ₹1,000 crore PLI booked, but PLI is set to fade, EV margins ~9% face depreciation drag, and steel up 17% YoY, copper up 42%, rubber up 40%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Auto capacity rising from 66,000 to 82,000 units/month (+27%) by end-FY27 with Chakan NU_IQ adding ~8,000 and EV going 8,000 to 12,000 by Feb-March 2027, both under construction.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Auto capacity from 66k to 82k units/month (+27%) by end-FY27 and 92k in FY28 against waiting periods of 5-7 months, while tractor industry flat and Farm profit fell 9%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Nagpur plant (1,500-2,000 acres) is already approved and land committed, and the company says it is effectively doubling capacity; Last Mile Mobility full-platform expansion is under evaluation at 45,000 units/quarter capped.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: SUV industry guided mid-to-high teens and LCV raised to double-digit growth, with 5-7 month waiting periods on Scorpio-N and XUV 7XO, but tractor offsets limit upside.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Tractor industry FY27 outlook already cut from +5% to flattish with H2 implying about -10%, and monsoon at 87% of LPA; Q3 expected to be pressured with a possible Q4 channel inventory correction.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Five major launches guided by June 2027 including first NU_IQ product, Lifestyler, a significant refresh and an LCV.

rows.label: Aerospace order book and third plant
rows.why: Airbus A320neo tail package and helicopter fuselage won, third plant under construction, and target of $1bn annual orders by FY30.

rows.label: Farm international subsidiary exits
rows.why: Sampo and Erkunt exits complete and Mitsubishi Mahindra Japan closing by Q4, so exit costs from last year's Q3 and Q4 will not recur, supporting H2 Farm consolidation.

rows.label: Mahindra Finance AUM growth
rows.why: AUM above ₹1,30,000 crore against ₹65,000 crore starting point, with PAT up 61% YoY on lower asset quality and tech gains.

tone.note: Management was confident on auto demand, capacity ramp and the PLI-supported quarter, but cautious on tractors, monsoon and commodity inflation; analysts pressed on margins and EV profitability, and management declined to share order book data.
